column1: # bin/lib/reachability-exemptions.tsv — the ONLY licence for a bin/ executable that no
# live entry point can reach. Read by bin/lib/reachability.sh; enforced by
# test/bin-reachability-gate.test.sh; reported by bin/heimdall-deadcode.
# FORMAT (tab-separated, three columns, one row per name):
#     name <TAB> recheck-by (YYYY-MM-DD) <TAB> reason
# WHY EVERY ROW EXPIRES. An exemption that never expires is a second way to go quietly
# dead. Someone writes "standalone by design" once, nobody looks again, and the binary
# rots under cover of its own excuse — which is exactly how bin/heimdall-brief would
# have survived even WITH a reachability gate. So the date is not decoration: past it,
# the gate FAILS until a human wires the tool up, deletes it, or re-justifies it with a
# new date. Four rot conditions are enforced against this file, not one:
#     MALFORMED  no name, no reason, or a recheck date that is not a real ISO date
#     EXPIRED    past its recheck date
#     STALE      the name is reachable again, so the exclusion is now hiding nothing
#     ORPHAN     bin/<name> no longer exists, and a leftover row would silently
#                pre-clear a future executable that reuses the name
# THIS FILE IS NOT A REFERENCE SURFACE. It names every exempt executable, so if the
# scanner read it, writing an exemption would MAKE the binary look reachable and the
# escape hatch would become the defect. reach_build() excludes it from the node set and
# the scan set; test/bin-reachability-gate.test.sh §3c proves the exclusion holds.
# RE-VERIFIED 2026-08-08. The gate previously carried its own flat "does any file name
# it?" matcher and reported the nine BY DESIGN / KNOWN GAP names below as "now wired —
# remove these rows". They are not wired. Every one of them was re-checked against a
# live entry point and every one is still unreachable; the flat matcher was reading
# mentions from other dead files as proof of life. The rows stay. If you meet that
# "stale, remove them" claim again, re-run `heimdall-deadcode --why <name>` before
# deleting anything — a row removed on a false staleness report silently converts an
# acknowledged dead tool into an unacknowledged one.
# THREE HONEST CATEGORIES. Only the first is a compliment.
#     BY DESIGN   no runtime caller is possible or wanted — a human runs it directly.
#     KNOWN GAP   it SHOULD be wired and is not. Recorded rather than hidden.
#     DEAD        unreachable, found by the 2026-08-08 transitive-liveness audit and
#                 not yet triaged. Recorded so the ratchet can hold against NEW dead
#                 code while these are decided. Short recheck window on purpose.
